task.title: Materialize claimed schedules atomically
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/799 by binding one claimed schedule to one caller-identified active task without a persistence crash gap.
acceptance_criteria: Atomically append schedule materialization and existing task start evidence with exact schedule and no-stream task guards.
Preserve exact immutable goal and caller-owned task identity in both projections through reopen.
Reject invalid schedule states, colliding task IDs, racing materializations, malformed payloads, and impossible histories without partial writes.
Create only inert task state without session, workflow, provider, tool, dispatch, retry, or permission authority.

attempts.diagnostic: Public integration tests failed because materialize, materialized status, task binding, and typed state errors did not exist.
attempts.patch: Added success/reopen, invalid-state, task collision, race, no-orphan, malformed-history, and due-exclusion tests.

attempts.diagnostic: Sequential schedule and task writes could leave one-sided durable state after a process or persistence failure.
attempts.patch: Reused the event log pair append to commit schedule.materialized and task.started atomically under exact aggregate expectations.

attempts.summary: Preserved review findings as bounded follow-up work.
attempts.diagnostic: Hosted review identified duplicated claimed-state preconditions between release and materialize and a missing explicit session-creation documentation exclusion.
attempts.patch: Kept materialization behavior bounded, recorded the shared-precondition refactor as issue 801, and preserved the complete inert authority contract in subsequent scheduler documentation.

outcome.summary: A claimed schedule can now become exactly one active task atomically, with no orphan schedule or task and no implied execution grant.

verification.command: nix develop --command cargo test --locked -p vela-kernel --test schedule_store

lessons: Two aggregate writes representing one binding decision need one atomic transaction rather than compensation.
Reuse existing authoritative task start events instead of creating a second scheduled-task lifecycle.
Task materialization is durable state creation, not permission to execute the task.
Review found duplicated claimed-state preconditions; the atomicity patch deferred that structural change to bounded follow-up issue 801.
Review also found that the ADR omitted session creation from one inert-boundary sentence; issue 801 explicitly tracked and corrected that documentation gap.
